{{short description|Result concerning the holomorphic extensions In several complex variables}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Ohsawa–Takegoshi ''L''<sup>2</sup> extension theorem}}

In [[several complex variables]], the '''Ohsawa–Takegoshi ''L''<sup>2</sup> extension theorem''' is a fundamental result concerning the [[Holomorphic function#Several variables|holomorphic]] extension of an [[Square-integrable function|<math>L^2</math>]]-holomorphic function defined on a bounded [[Stein manifold]] (such as a [[pseudoconvex]] [[compact (mathematics)|compact]] set in <math>\mathbb{C}^n</math> of dimension less than <math>n</math>) to a domain of higher dimension, with a bound on the growth. It was discovered by [[Takeo Ohsawa]] and Kensho Takegoshi in 1987,<ref>{{harvtxt|Ohsawa|Takegoshi|1987}}</ref> using what have been described as ''ad hoc'' methods involving twisted [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]]s, but simpler proofs have since been discovered.<ref>{{harvtxt|Siu|2011}}</ref> One of the deepest result in complex analysis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.nagoya-u.ac.jp/~x10001c/L2estimate.pdf
|title=Hörmander's L2－estimate and the Ohsawa-Takegoshi extension theorem by Bo-Yong Chen Young mathematician workshop on SCV July 24-July 27, 2013, Nagoya|accessdate=2026-07-28|page=7}}</ref> Many generalizations and similar results exist, and are known as theorems of Ohsawa–Takegoshi type.
